# aiflow — full reference for LLMs

> Self-contained explanation of what aiflow is and how it works, for AI assistants and context7.
> aiflow turns any repository into a governed, AI-driven software-delivery pipeline — agent-agnostic
> across Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and OpenAI Codex CLI.
> Version 0.8.0 · MIT · https://github.com/Cyber93de/aiflow · docs https://cyber93de.github.io/aiflow/

## What aiflow is
A cross-platform CLI (POSIX bash + a Windows PowerShell launcher) that bootstraps and governs
AI-agent-driven projects. It wires whichever coding agent(s) you use — Claude Code (full feature
set: subagents, hooks, slash-commands), GitHub Copilot, and/or OpenAI Codex CLI — plus an
agent-agnostic Ralph loop (open-ralph-wiggum) that works with all three — to durable task memory,
two-layer code memory, specialist agents/Skills, team collaboration, gitflow
release automation, and token savings — with one command. It is project-scoped (secrets and
settings live in the project, never globally), token-based (never OAuth for git hosts), and
vendor-neutral (your own Anthropic API key or Claude Code OAuth token). It vendors nothing; it
installs/invokes external tools.

## Agent-agnostic core
`AGENTS.md` at the repo root is the single, shared source of truth (code style, quality gates,
task workflow, git rules, Definition of Done) any coding agent should read. `CLAUDE.md` is a
one-line `@AGENTS.md` import (Claude Code's native memory-import syntax) so Claude Code loads the
identical content. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` points GitHub Copilot at `AGENTS.md`; OpenAI
Codex CLI reads `AGENTS.md` directly by convention (no pointer needed). Sections in `AGENTS.md`
marked "(Claude Code only)" — subagents, hooks, slash-commands, caveman/rtk — are
automation only Claude Code can dispatch in-session; every other agent follows the same rules
manually. `.aiflow/config.json`'s `agents{claude,copilot,codex}` (any combination, Claude Code on
by default) selects which agent-specific files get rendered: `.mcp.json` (Claude), `.codex/
config.toml` (Codex, TOML `[mcp_servers.*]`), `.vscode/mcp.json` (Copilot) — all from the same MCP
server set (`mcp.*`, `remote.mcp`, `gitkraken.enabled`).

## How it works (the pipeline)
1. `aiflow init` (or `change-settings`) runs an interactive Q&A and writes `.aiflow/config.json` —
   the single source of truth.
2. `lib/apply.sh` reads that config and idempotently RENDERS: `.mcp.json` (enabled MCP servers +
   the git-host MCP for your remote), git branching + hooks (git only), the Beads↔host sync config,
   `.claude/memory/*` (project-aim, dev-environment, memory-policy), `.aiflow/router-config.json`
   (Ollama/cost providers), `.aiflow/team-prefs.json`, and `.aiflow/bd-close-sync.sh`.
3. `lib/install-deps.sh` installs only the enabled tools (user-space).

## Windows prerequisites (before anything else)
aiflow's own CLI runs in PowerShell + Git Bash. Anything that COMPILES NATIVE CODE (C/C++,
`node-gyp`, Python C-extensions, `uv`-built tools) must run in WSL, never MinGW/MSYS2 — two
parallel toolchains cause ABI/header mismatches, `PATH` collisions between the two `sh.exe`s, and
builds that differ from Linux CI. Required setup, in order: (1) enable hardware virtualisation in
the BIOS/UEFI — Intel VT-x, AMD SVM Mode; (2) `wsl --install` in an admin PowerShell (enables WSL +
Virtual Machine Platform), reboot; (3) `wsl --install -d Ubuntu`, start it once, confirm
`wsl -l -v` reports VERSION 2; (4) inside WSL `sudo apt install -y build-essential` for gcc/g++,
plus `cmake`/`python3-dev`/a cross-toolchain as the project needs. Projects that compile native
code should live inside the WSL filesystem, not under `/mnt/c`. `aiflow doctor` reports all four
steps on Windows and never installs MinGW.

Every script a project invokes on its own (Claude Code hooks, `.aiflow/*` checks, `docker/run.*`)
ships as a `.sh` + `.ps1` pair; `apply.sh` picks the interpreter per `dev.os` when writing
`.claude/settings.json`'s hook commands — Windows projects need no Git-Bash for their own
hooks/checks. `aiflow update` self-updates the CLI install: `git pull --ff-only` if `AIFLOW_HOME`
is a git checkout; otherwise it checks the GitHub Releases API for a newer version, downloads the
matching per-OS archive, verifies it against the published `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and installs it over
`AIFLOW_HOME`. `aiflow project-update` refreshes one project from the installed templates:
mechanical scripts (`.aiflow/*`, `.claude/hooks/*`, `docker/run.*`, `.github/scripts/*`) always,
plus agent definitions
(`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/agents/*`,
`.claude/commands/*`, `.claude/skills/*`), the git hooks (`.githooks/*`) and
`.aiflow/router-config.example.json` — any of those that was customised (differs from the
incoming template) is renamed to `<file>.bak` first, never deleted, and reported so you can
reapply your changes; identical files are overwritten silently. Nothing is ever deleted: a script
the templates no longer ship is listed at the end of the run (for `.aiflow/` and `.claude/hooks/`;
`.github/scripts/` is shared, so project-owned scripts there are not flagged). Never touches `.beads/`,
`.claude/memory/*`, `.github/workflows/*` (yours to extend — a shipped CI helper that no workflow
calls yet is advised at the end of the run, never written in), or your `.aiflow/config.json`
project settings (aim, architecture) — only
`meta.aiflowVersion` is stamped (each project stamps the aiflow version it was generated with, and
is prompted to upgrade when it falls behind the installed CLI).

## Code memory (the differentiator)
Two complementary indexes plus durable task memory. The agent routes each question to the cheapest
source that answers it (written to `.claude/memory/memory-policy.md`):
- Beads (`bd`) — current task, dependencies, decisions, session state (Dolt-backed, survives compaction).
- memory files — durable prose facts.
- graphify (MCP) — STRUCTURAL code graph: where a symbol is defined, who calls it, dependency direction.
- cocoindex-code / `ccc` (MCP) — SEMANTIC RAG: "find code about concept X"; AST-aware, local
  embeddings (sentence-transformers, no API key), ~70% fewer tokens than reading files; incremental.
- context7 (MCP) — external, version-correct library/framework docs.
Rule: never scan whole files first; use graph + RAG to locate the few relevant chunks, then open only
those. `aiflow index` refreshes BOTH indexes (graphify build + ccc index).

## Remote hosts (token-based)
`remote.type` ∈ github | github-enterprise | gitlab | gitlab-self | bitbucket | forgejo | gitea |
custom | none. The matching host MCP is wired automatically with the base URL threaded in
(GITHUB_HOST / GITLAB_API_URL / GITEA_URL). Token comes from `.env` via `remote.tokenEnv`
(e.g. GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, GIT_REMOTE_TOKEN). No OAuth for git hosts. Each host also gets a
predefined release-publish CI workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`,
`.gitea/workflows/release.yml`, `.forgejo/workflows/release.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`) —
written once, never overwritten if one already exists — that publishes a release entry/note when
a version tag is pushed (sources in `release-workflows/`, outside `templates/`). `gitkraken.
enabled` wires the GitKraken MCP (via the `gk` CLI) independently of the host choice, since
GitKraken is a client, not a host.

## Models
- Claude access: `claude.auth` = apikey (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or oauth (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN).
- Ollama: local models, no key; `aiflow ollama add|pull|list`; qwen3-coder recommended. Selected
  models are written into `.aiflow/router-config.json` and used via `aiflow shell --router`.
- More/cloud models via claude-code-router (~/.claude-code-router/config.json): DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Gemini.
- Model tiers per activity (`modelRouting`, Claude Code only, on by default): `aiflow apply` stamps
  a `model:` line into each subagent's frontmatter by the KIND of work. reasoning = opus (or fable):
  architect, planner, reviewer, security-advisor, requirements-check, modernization-advisor,
  orchestrator. implementation = sonnet: implementer, tester, quality-check, accessibility-checker.
  mechanical = haiku: docs-sync, test-gap-advisor, dependency-auditor, performance-advisor,
  onboarder. Override per tier via `modelRouting.tiers.<tier>` or per agent via
  `modelRouting.agents.<name> = <tier>`; both survive `aiflow change-settings`.
  `modelRouting.enabled:false` strips every `model:` line. Escalate a tier when a task turns out to
  touch the architecture; never silently downgrade.

## Team collaboration
Beads issues live in a shared Dolt database synced over `refs/dolt/data` on the git remote — one issue
graph, no extra server. Rules: session-start auto-pull (`bd dolt pull` hook), atomic claiming
(`bd ready --claim` / `bd update --claim`, prevents double-grab), pull-before-push
(`aiflow sync`, `aiflow close-sync`), never force-push, conflicts resolved via `bd dolt pull`.
Queue mode (AGENTS.md §4b): Beads is an authoritative work queue — closing a bead ends a task, not the
session. The agent refreshes the queue (`aiflow next`, ranked: priority → unblocks-most → continuation
of the bead just closed) and continues; it stops only when nothing is actionable, everything left is
blocked, the user says stop, or a decision/credential only the user has is required. A Claude Code
`Stop` hook (`.claude/hooks/queue-continue.*`) hands the next task back once; opt out via
`beads.queueMode = false` or `AIFLOW_QUEUE_MODE=off`.

## Agents
The network: /orchestrate is the entry point for anything that is not a single obvious edit. The
orchestrator owns the route and never implements: planner (goal -> dependency-ordered beads with AC
and a recommended agent per bead, returned as a HANDOFF block) -> architect when the change crosses
module/layer boundaries or AGENTS.md section 2b still has no rules ("Rule zero") -> implementer ->
tester when the pre-analysis flags risk -> reviewer (always; PASS closes the bead, CHANGES REQUIRED
goes back to the implementer). Exactly ONE specialist per bead at a time, and every handover is
written into the bead (`bd update <id> --notes "route: ..."`) so it survives /compact. The audit
agents are outside this loop: manually triggered, they only file prefixed beads (or, for
modernization-advisor, a report for the architect), and those beads re-enter the route at the top.
Every agent file carries a "Net & handoffs" section naming who it receives from and hands to, so a
standalone-started agent still knows where its output belongs. Without Claude Code the route is
identical, just manual.
Orchestrator: entry point/dispatcher, routes and evaluates, escalates PO decisions to the user,
turns discovered work into beads (--deps discovered-from:), never writes code/tests/docs/ADRs.
Delivery: architect, planner, implementer (senior engineer: mandatory pre-analysis of architecture
fit/effort/complexity before code, targeted refactoring, SOLID/DRY/KISS/YAGNI, testable by design,
proven frameworks + design patterns over self-built, PO-level questions with recorded decisions),
reviewer (architect AND quality gate in one: architecture integrity + ADRs, design, tech debt,
vulnerabilities, concurrency, breaking changes, plus an objective release checklist; PASS/CHANGES
REQUIRED; suggestions persisted as beads), tester (test/QA engineer: negative/edge/boundary/
exception/invalid-input + test-quality audit; runs adaptively on high risk/complexity).
All delivery agents: production-ready output only (low-maturity tech flagged by reviewer+tester),
small classes/KISS (divide & conquer + interfaces; utility-lib overloads excepted), monolith
avoidance (service-ready seams), state-of-the-art check (SOAP-vs-REST, XML-vs-JSON, legacy MQ
questioned as PO decisions), deliberate Redis/SQLite/Elasticsearch consideration for perf/search.
Audit (file Beads issues): security-advisor, quality-check, dependency-auditor, test-gap-advisor,
performance-advisor, docs-sync, accessibility-checker (aiflow a11y-check: strict WCAG 2.2 AA ->
[accessibility] beads + recommends axe-core/Pa11y/Lighthouse CI for the E2E suite; not in the
loop), requirements-check (report only), modernization-advisor (aiflow modernize-check: brownfield
modernisation concepts as report .aiflow/modernization-report.md for the architect — EOL stacks,
monolith->microservices strangler-fig, legacy->REST/JSON+cloud-native eventing, svn->git, missing
unit/BDD/E2E frameworks; report only, not in the loop). Brownfield: onboarder (learns the codebase into
memory/AGENTS.md/arc42 and proposes a project aim from its understanding — user must confirm it).
Shipped agents are deliberately generic (strong universal base config, ~70-80% less setup than
blank); customise them per project in .claude/agents/*.md (Claude Code only — Copilot/Codex follow
the same roles manually from AGENTS.md §5). The project aim (.claude/memory/project-aim.md +
AGENTS.md §1, set via init/change-settings) tunes the agent to the project — 2-4 sentences: what,
for whom, target architecture, quality bar. Slash-commands (Claude Code only): /orchestrate (entry point), /intake-issue,
/decompose, /plan-epic, /implement [bead] [ralph|no-ralph], /review-ac, /arch, the audit commands,
/onboard, /explain, /standup. Skills (Claude Code only, `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) —
distinct from slash-commands: Claude Code matches a skill's description against the current task
and offers to run it automatically. Skill vs agent: an AGENT is a role (who acts, with what
authority, in what order, what it hands to whom) and lives in .claude/agents/*.md; a SKILL is
knowledge several roles need (a checklist, the trade-offs of a technology) and lives in
.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md. Both may exist for one topic — the same-named agent then uses the skill
instead of restating it. Rules that must fire on EVERY task (section 2 architecture rules, sections
3a/3b/3c quality gates) stay inline in AGENTS.md, because a skill is offered by pattern match and
Copilot/Codex get no auto-offer at all. Frontmatter must be valid YAML and nothing warns you if it
isn't: an agent with an unparseable block is silently dropped from the roster, a command/skill
falls back to its body text as the description and stops matching its trigger words. Usual cause is
an unquoted `description:` containing a colon+space — quote it. The generated project's pre-commit
hook enforces this on staging and CI on every push, both via .github/scripts/check-frontmatter.py
(needs python3/python + PyYAML; the hook skips with a note when they are missing, CI does not).
Technology-stack skills: stack-embedded (C/C++ firmware — HAL/driver separation, no allocation
after init, ISR discipline, watchdog, deterministic timing, cross-toolchain in WSL on Windows, host
unit tests against a mocked HAL); stack-mobile (Flutter/Dart, Kotlin/Android, Swift/iOS —
UI->presentation->domain<-data layering, one state-management choice, process death, offline/sync,
Keystore/Keychain, store constraints); stack-web-frontend (Angular/React/Vue — feature slices,
server state vs client state, DTO->view-model mapping, XSS and token handling, Core Web Vitals
budgets, i18n, a11y, Testing-Library + Playwright); stack-backend (Spring/Quarkus/Jakarta, .NET,
Rust, Node, Go, Python — hexagonal layering with ports, transaction boundaries, 12-factor config,
timeouts/retries/circuit breakers, observability, FOSS-first: PostgreSQL, Tomcat, Keycloak,
Prometheus; Testcontainers over in-memory doubles).
Integration/data skills: api-design (REST versioning, status codes, pagination, idempotency,
problem+json, OpenAPI, .http files per section 3b; when SOAP is legitimate and how to migrate off
it; GraphQL and gRPC trade-offs); messaging-events (when async beats synchronous; Kafka/RabbitMQ/
NATS/SQS; at-least-once + idempotent consumers; transactional outbox; ordering/partitioning; schema
registry compatibility; DLQs; sagas over distributed transactions); data-storage (relational
default per section 3c, when NoSQL is actually justified, embedded DBs SQLite/Room/Drift/Realm,
Redis as cache with designed invalidation and mandatory TTLs, Elasticsearch as a DERIVED read layer
fed from the outbox — never the source of truth, indexing and expand-contract migrations);
cloud-native (multi-stage non-root pinned images, 12-factor, K8s liveness vs readiness, resource
limits, PodDisruptionBudget, secret stores, EC2 immutable images, modular monolith before
microservices, observability and cost).
Cross-cutting: security (OWASP Top 10 as the review raster + ASVS levels; IAM least privilege with
roles not per-user grants, short-lived/workload credentials over static keys, rotation; API authN/
authZ per section 3b incl. JWT alg/exp/aud/iss validation; secrets never in code/image/log/URL;
supply chain — pinned lockfiles, CI scanning, vetted dependencies, never curl-pipe-sh unverified).
The security-advisor agent uses this same raster so findings read identically wherever they came
from.
Also ships seo-optimization: SEO for any web-facing
project/framework (HTML, GitHub Pages, static sites, Next.js, Astro, Hugo, Jekyll, VuePress,
VitePress, React, Vue, Svelte, Angular) — meta tags, Open Graph/Twitter Cards, JSON-LD structured
data, robots.txt/sitemap.xml, canonical URLs, Core Web Vitals, GitHub Pages specifics; ends with
an SEO report. Also ships ponytail: a YAGNI decision ladder (needed? already in the codebase?
stdlib? platform feature? installed dependency? one-liner? only then write it) applied before new
code/dependencies/abstractions; off by default, toggle via ponytail.enabled/.mode
(full/lite/ultra); /ponytail-review audits a diff for over-engineering regardless of the toggle.
Also ships memory-setup: the full memory/context-routing stack (Beads/memory files/graphify/
cocoindex-code/context7 priority order, team-prefs, Ollama routing) — AGENTS.md §8 keeps only the
toggle + essentials, the rest lives in this skill. REST/Database rules (§3b/§3c, MANDATORY) and
the Ralph-loop decision rule (§6, needed every task) stay inline in AGENTS.md rather than moving
to a skill, since skills are Claude-Code-only and pattern-matched (not guaranteed to fire), which
would risk silently dropping enforcement for Codex/Copilot and for rules needed on every task.
Autonomy: the Ralph loop (open-ralph-wiggum, agent-agnostic: Claude Code/Codex
CLI/Copilot CLI via `--agent`; interactive `/ralph-loop` is Claude Code-only; headless
`aiflow ralph` / CI works with any); if not specified, the implementer decides from its
pre-analysis.

## Architecture rules (AGENTS.md section 2, MANDATORY, every language)
Layered architecture with an inward dependency direction: presentation/API -> application/service
-> domain <- infrastructure. No layer skips; the domain imports nothing outward (no ORM
annotations, HTTP types or vendor SDKs on entities); no cyclic dependencies. Embedded equivalent:
application <-> service <-> HAL/driver, business logic never touches a register. Interfaces at
every seam: the domain declares the port, infrastructure provides the adapter, wired by dependency
injection, never `new`-ed in the caller. DAO/repository is the only place that talks to a data
store (no SQL/ORM/file access elsewhere), one per aggregate. DTOs carry anything across a process
boundary (REST/SOAP/queue/UI) and are mapped explicitly; domain objects never leave the domain —
an entity annotated for both persistence and JSON is a review finding. Reuse before duplication;
generics/type parameters to remove duplication, not to build speculative layers. Complexity is
actively avoided: small single-purpose methods, guard clauses over nesting, no god classes.
Section 2b holds the project's concrete decisions. Section 2c: rules must exist — if 2b is still a
placeholder the architect establishes a set (its "Rule zero") into 2b AND an ADR; once recorded
they change only via a superseding ADR; a task that does not fit is NOT implemented as-is — the
agent stops before coding, asks in PO language with options + consequences, and the decision is
recorded. The reviewer treats each rule as a BLOCKER, the implementer as an abort criterion.

## Quality, git, releases
Google style for all languages; Conventional Commits; pre-commit/commit-msg/pre-push enforcement
hooks. Quality gates on every implementation: static analysis (tool or agent-performed — no code
smells), >80 % line coverage + all non-static methods tested, unit + BDD end-to-end tests always
(integration/system where sensible; BDD for E2E/system/acceptance), leveled logging mandatory;
REST APIs are versioned from day one (/api/v1/...; breaking -> new version + deprecation window)
and properly secured — Basic Auth is insufficient: OAuth2/OIDC, short-lived JWT, or managed API
keys with rotation; authorisation per endpoint. REST endpoints ship IDE-testable .http files
(host/port/test credentials from .env). Ralph loop: implementer decides automatically from its
pre-analysis; manual triggers win (/implement <bead> ralph|no-ralph, or a directive written into
the issue itself). Token framing: saving is a goal but partially achieved per task due to quality
rules; net win = production-ready on first pass, no re-prompting/rework. Database
rules (AGENTS.md §3c): NEW data models >=3NF, real foreign keys, junction tables for m:n, NOT NULL
default, CHECK/UNIQUE constraints, precise types, no magic values, only necessary indexes, lookup
tables, deliberate cascades, soft delete where needed (R1-R20); EXISTING schemas are handled with
care (B1-B8 cautionary guidance): they may be shared by other projects and must support rollback
to older app versions — never restructure/re-key/re-type/merge/split/normalise as a side effect;
note improvement potential as recommendation beads; commissioned schema changes are high-risk work
(external-consumer check, backward-compat/rollback plan, versioned migration). Uncommissioned
structural changes in a feature diff = review BLOCKER. Branching models: simple | gitflow | none, PR-only, auto-release, SemVer/CalVer; enforced by
hooks + `aiflow protect` + `aiflow release`. Gitflow: `feature/*`/`bugfix/*` from develop only,
`hotfix/*` from main (`aiflow hotfix <name>`, versions `X.Y.(Z+1)-HOTFIX`); only develop, hotfix/*,
or chore/* may ever reach main; chore/* never releases; main may never carry a
`-SNAPSHOT`/`-HOTFIX` version; releasing always needs explicit human confirmation
(`aiflow release --yes`).

## Token optimization
Per-agent: Claude Code gets caveman (terse output, ~75% fewer output tokens; code/commits/security
stay normal) and rtk (CLI-output filtering, 60–90% fewer), both ON by default. GitHub Copilot gets
the token-optimization guide (github.com/olivomarco/github-copilot-token-optimization) baked into
`.github/copilot-instructions.md` — terse output, "landmines only" context files, stable
model/tool-set per thread. OpenAI Codex CLI gets optional CodexSaver
(github.com/fendouai/CodexSaver, `codexsaver.enabled`) — an MCP server routing cheap/bounded work
to a cheaper worker, needs a provider API key. Agent-agnostic: graph/RAG retrieval instead of
reading whole files; cheap/local model routing. Measure with `aiflow cost` (ccusage).
`/compact` is a rule, not a suggestion (AGENTS.md section 9): compact right after `aiflow init`
(greenfield — the Q&A already wrote aim/stack/architecture into config + memory), right after the
onboarder (brownfield — its findings are in `.claude/memory/`, AGENTS.md section 1/2 and arc42),
after every closed bead, and before a long Ralph run or big refactor. Persist first (bead notes,
memory file, ADR), then compact — compaction is not storage. Copilot/Codex: start a fresh thread at
the same four points.

## Containers & CI/CD
Headless container runs via `docker/run.sh` using Podman OR Docker (auto-detected; `AIFLOW_CONTAINER`
override). CI/CD is GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` (validate + dry-run build), `release.yml` (tag + per-OS
archives on VERSION bump), `pages.yml` (deploy docs). No Dagger.

## Key commands
init · install-deps · change-settings · shell [--router] · sync [pull|push|both] · close-sync <id> ·
next [--after <id>] [--claim] [--json] (next ready bead, queue mode) ·
ollama [pull|add|list] · index · ralph "<prompt|bead>" · onboard · security-check / quality-check /
requirements-check / dependency-check / test-gap / perf-check / docs-check · hotfix <name> ·
release [--yes] [--push] · protect · cost · doctor · upgrade · update · project-update · version.

## Config schema (essentials)
.aiflow/config.json fields: caveman{enabled,mode}, rtk{enabled}, ponytail{enabled,mode}, router{enabled}, graphify{enabled},
taskmaster{enabled}, mcp{filesystem,context7,cocoindex}, memory{enabled,graph,intensity=off|light|
normal|aggressive}, agents{claude,copilot,codex} (which agent-specific files get rendered),
modelRouting{enabled,tiers{reasoning,implementation,mechanical},agents{<name>:<tier>}},
claude{auth}, vcs{system=git|svn|none}, remote{type,baseUrl,api,tokenEnv,mcp},
gitkraken{enabled}, codexsaver{enabled,provider,apiKeyEnv}, sync{askOnClose,pullOnStart}, ollama{enabled,url,models},
teamPrefs{enabled,codeStyle}, project{aim,architecture}, dev{os,ide},
git{model,strict,prOnly,autoRelease,versionStrategy,releaseTags,chore},
meta{aiflowVersion} (stamped at init; compared against the installed CLI's VERSION to offer
`aiflow project-update`).
